The Discharger thickens secondary sludge with a dissolved air flotation unit, combines secondary sludge with primary sludge that it treats with lime, and dewaters the combined sludge with centrifuges.

The Discharger incinerates the final dewatered sludge onsite, which produces ash.
The Discharger hires a contractor to truck the ash to an offsite recycling facility for use as a soil amendment.

If Facility incinerators are inoperable, the Discharger may haul biosolids to a landfill, an organic materials recovery facility, or the East Bay Municipal Utility District wastewater treatment plant.

Planned Changes. The Discharger continues to promote and support recycled water planning efforts in conjunction with local water agencies. This includes leading the continued evaluation of the Refinery Recycled Water Exchange Project – an advanced recycled water treatment project (including nutrient removal) that would produce approximately 13.5 MGD of recycled water for the Contra Costa Water District to serve to its two existing refinery customers.
